title: Explain the Importance of Basic Network Security Concepts

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Network security protects data, identities, devices, access, physical equipment, network segments, and regulatory obligations.
bullets: Encryption, certificates, PKI, and self-signed certificates
IAM, authentication, authorization, MFA, SSO, RADIUS, LDAP, SAML, TACACS+, and time-based authentication
Risk, vulnerability, exploit, threat, and the CIA triad
Data locality, PCI DSS, GDPR, and network segmentation
sections.callout: PROTECT DATA → VERIFY IDENTITY → CONTROL ACCESS → PROTECT EQUIPMENT → DETECT THREATS → SEGMENT RISK

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a security requirement appears, determine whether it protects data, proves identity, controls permissions, secures physical infrastructure, manages risk, satisfies compliance, or isolates devices.
bullets: Identity bound to a public key → Certificate

sections.title: Encryption, Certificates, and PKI

entries.title: Encryption
paragraphs: Encryption changes readable data into a protected form. Data in transit is moving across a network; data at rest is stored in files, databases, backups, or configurations.

entries.title: Digital Certificate
paragraphs: A certificate associates an identity with a cryptographic public key and supports secure connections and identity verification.
entries.memoryHook: This public key belongs to this identity.

entries.title: Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)
paragraphs: PKI creates, manages, distributes, validates, and revokes certificates, forming the broader certificate trust system.

entries.title: Self-Signed Certificate
paragraphs: A self-signed certificate is signed by the entity that created it instead of an externally trusted certificate authority. It can encrypt traffic, but clients may not trust it automatically.

sections.callout: Credential binding identity to a key → Certificate. System managing certificate trust → PKI.

sections.title: Identity and Access Management (IAM)
paragraphs: IAM manages digital identities and their access to resources. Authentication asks who you are; authorization determines what an authenticated identity may do.

entries.title: Multifactor Authentication (MFA)
paragraphs: MFA uses more than one factor category, such as something known, possessed, or inherent. Password plus authenticator code is MFA.
entries.memoryHook: More than one different type of proof.

entries.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
paragraphs: SSO lets a user authenticate once and reach multiple authorized services without repeatedly entering credentials.
entries.memoryHook: Sign in once; access multiple services.

entries.title: Time-Based Authentication
paragraphs: Time-based authentication uses short-lived codes that change according to time, such as authenticator-app one-time passwords.

sections.callout: Multiple factor types → MFA. One authentication reused across services → SSO.

sections.title: AAA, Directories, and Federation

entries.title: RADIUS
paragraphs: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service provides centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting for network access, including enterprise wireless, VPN, and NAC scenarios.

entries.title: LDAP
paragraphs: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol accesses and manages directory information such as users, groups, devices, and organizational objects.

entries.title: SAML
paragraphs: Security Assertion Markup Language exchanges identity and authentication assertions between systems and commonly supports federated web authentication and SSO.
entries.memoryHook: One system tells another the user is authenticated.

entries.title: TACACS+
paragraphs: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus provides centralized AAA strongly associated with administrator access to routers, switches, and other network infrastructure.

sections.callout: Network access → RADIUS. Network-device administration → TACACS+. Directory lookup → LDAP. Federated assertion → SAML.

sections.title: Authorization Controls

entries.title: Least Privilege
paragraphs: Least privilege grants only the permissions needed to perform required duties and removes unnecessary rights.

entries.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
paragraphs: RBAC assigns permissions according to job roles such as help desk, network administrator, HR, or finance.

entries.title: Geofencing
paragraphs: Geofencing applies access rules based on geographic location, such as rejecting authentication from unapproved regions.

sections.callout: Minimum required access → Least privilege. Access according to role → RBAC.

entries.title: Cameras and Locks
paragraphs: Cameras monitor and record physical activity. Locks restrict entry to rooms, racks, cabinets, and equipment.
entries.memoryHook: Watch the environment and keep unauthorized people out.

entries.title: Honeypot
paragraphs: A honeypot is one decoy system intentionally exposed to attract and observe malicious activity.

entries.title: Honeynet
paragraphs: A honeynet is a collection or network of deceptive systems that simulates a larger environment.

sections.title: Risk, Vulnerability, Exploit, and Threat

entries.title: Vulnerability
paragraphs: A vulnerability is a weakness, such as unpatched software, a weak configuration, or a default password.

entries.title: Exploit
paragraphs: An exploit is a method or technique that takes advantage of a vulnerability.

entries.title: Threat
paragraphs: A threat is a potential source of harm, including an attacker, malware, or environmental event.

entries.title: Risk
paragraphs: Risk represents potential loss when a threat can affect a vulnerable asset and is evaluated through likelihood and impact.
entries.memoryHook: What could happen, and how bad would it be?

sections.callout: Weakness → Vulnerability. Use it → Exploit. Danger → Threat. Potential loss → Risk.

entries.title: Confidentiality
paragraphs: Information is disclosed only to authorized identities. Encryption and access control support confidentiality.

entries.title: Integrity
paragraphs: Information remains accurate and changes only through authorized action.

entries.title: Availability
paragraphs: Systems and data remain accessible when needed. Redundancy and recovery support availability.

entries.title: Data Locality
paragraphs: Data locality concerns the physical or geographic region where information is stored and processed.

entries.title: PCI DSS
paragraphs: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard establishes security requirements for payment-card data.

entries.title: GDPR
paragraphs: General Data Protection Regulation governs personal-data protection and processing within its applicable jurisdiction.

sections.title: Network Segmentation Enforcement
paragraphs: Segmentation limits access and reduces the spread of compromise by separating device groups with different risks and trust levels.

entries.title: IoT and IIoT
paragraphs: Internet of Things devices include cameras, sensors, smart devices, and building systems. Industrial Internet of Things applies connected-device concepts to industrial settings; both can require isolation from general user networks.

entries.title: SCADA, ICS, and OT
paragraphs: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, Industrial Control Systems, and Operational Technology control physical processes and need strong segmentation from ordinary IT networks.

entries.title: Guest
paragraphs: Guest users should reach permitted services such as the Internet without reaching trusted internal systems.

entries.title: BYOD
paragraphs: Bring Your Own Device endpoints are personally owned and may not meet corporate management standards, so they receive controlled, segmented access.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Moving protected data → Encryption in transit
Stored protected data → Encryption at rest

entries.title: Data in Transit vs. Data at Rest
paragraphs: Moving → Transit. Stored → Rest.

entries.title: Certificate vs. PKI
paragraphs: Identity/public-key credential → Certificate. Trust-management framework → PKI.

entries.title: Authentication vs. Authorization
paragraphs: Who are you? → Authentication. What may you do? → Authorization.

entries.title: MFA vs. SSO
paragraphs: Multiple factors → MFA. One authentication reused across services → SSO.

entries.title: RADIUS vs. TACACS+
paragraphs: Network access → RADIUS. Device administration → TACACS+.

entries.title: LDAP vs. SAML
paragraphs: Directory access → LDAP. Federated assertions → SAML.

entries.title: Least Privilege vs. RBAC
paragraphs: Minimum needed access → Least privilege. Access based on role → RBAC.

entries.title: Honeypot vs. Honeynet
paragraphs: One decoy → Honeypot. Network of decoys → Honeynet.

entries.title: Vulnerability vs. Exploit
paragraphs: Weakness → Vulnerability. Technique using it → Exploit.

entries.title: Threat vs. Risk
paragraphs: Potential danger → Threat. Potential impact or loss → Risk.

entries.title: CIA Triad
paragraphs: Unauthorized disclosure → Confidentiality. Unauthorized alteration → Integrity. Unreachable service → Availability.

entries.title: IoT vs. IIoT/OT
paragraphs: General connected embedded device → IoT. Industrial connected environment → IIoT or OT.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: PROTECT DATA → VERIFY IDENTITY → CONTROL ACCESS → PROTECT EQUIPMENT → DETECT THREATS → SEGMENT RISK
